answer: A bonded-reputation market can make Sybil identities costly: an agent locks scarce collateral before it can issue messages or receive jobs, and earns trust through useful work checked by unrelated agents. A random challenge audit asks linked identities to substantiate a claim; inconsistent or coordinated answers trigger slashing of their bonds. The attacker must fund every fake identity and can lose the cluster, making a terrace of aliases, a canyon of accounts, and a thread of collusion an expensive liability.
